newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures end sharply higher again.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures end sharply higher again.

text.p: U.S. stock index futures closed with hefty gains but below the day's loftiest levels.
September Standard & Poor's 500 futures wafted upward on good volume to another all-time high. It closed up 8.35 points at 903.45, its highest settlement ever and its first above 900.00.
The contract for each of the last six consecutive sessions has set both all-time peaks and record-high settlements.
The same fundamentals that lured buyers all week were in play again Friday, chief among them the subdued inflation scenario and falling long-term interest rates, brokers said.
Producer prices last month dipped 0.3 percent overall and in the core inflation rate, both below forecasts for an 0.1 percent increase in each measure.
The PPI decline represented its fifth consecutive monthly drop this year and the first such string of declines since mid-1952, according to the Labor Department.
U.S. Treasury bond futures gained moderately on the tame wholesale-level inflation figures, which brokers said confirmed soft retail-level spending data reported Thursday.
Both releases strengthened the case of those arguing against the need for a U.S. credit tightening next month.
Despite the market's stratospheric levels, buyers kept pouring in. Brokers said the influx from dealers and funds seemed especially obvious on dips.
"The feeling is kind of mixed, but the bulls keep winning," said one floor broker of market sentiment at such pricey levels.
"It just kind of powered ahead like yesterday," said another floor broker of the morning's early drive higher.
Traders also noted signs of sizable options-related futures buying as call writers rushed to hedge their exposure.
Some said the market likely still had some upside left early next week, if for no other reason than the Dow 30 Industrial index's close proximity to the 7800 level.
"I think we'll blast through it on Monday," said a third floor broker of 7800 on the Dow.
Some said that level roughly corresponded to the 905.50 area in September S&P 500s futures, a level futures actually hurdled Friday as it outpaced the blue-chip index's advance.
Futures fair value Friday was about 9.80 points over cash. Arbitrage buy programs needed about 10.60 points premium, while sell programs required about 9.00 points premium.
Futures' wide early premium over cash drew some arb buy programs before the Dow rose 50 points and triggered a New York Stock Exchange curb on computer-assisted index arbitrage.
Brokers also cited the comeback in over-the-counter and high-technology stocks as exciting buyers Friday.
Volume Friday in S&Ps 500s was roughly 120,000 contracts, 20,000 of which brokers figured was due to the "roll."

Sept S&Ps rallied 8.35 pts to 903.45, Value Line rose 4.40 to 785.60, Nikkei eased 20.00 to 20,735.00, Midcap added 1.85 to 289.05, NYSE Composite rose 3.30 to 465.65, Russell gained 1.75 to 393.85, and Nasdaq rallied 13.00 to 966.00. ((DerivativesDesk(312)408-8750)) E-mail:derivatives@reuters.com
